<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par109 />{{GHGheb|text=אַל־נָא}}); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ אַל־יֵרָא|translate=neither let any man be seen!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=7}} ''be not'' ({{GHGheb|text=אַל־תְּהִי}}) ''wise in thine own eyes!'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=31}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־יַֽאֲמֵן|translate=ne confidat}}. In the form of a request (prayer), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּשְׁחֵת|translate=destroy not!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=27|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=18|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|109|d}}
Rem. 1. The few examples of {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the jussive could at most have arisen from the attempt to moderate subsequently by means of the jussive (voluntative) form what was at first intended to be a strict command ({{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with imperf. indic.); probably, however, they are either cases in which the defective writing has been misunderstood (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=48|verse=14}}), or (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=8}}) instances of the purely rhythmical jussive form treated below, under ''k''. Moreover, cf. {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יוֹסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=2}} and from the same verb {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=12}} (unless it is to be referred to ''h'') and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=1}}. The same form, however, appears also to stand three times for the cohortative (see below), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=19}} for the ordinary imperfect (but see below, ''i''). Thus it is doubtful whether an imaginary by-form of the ordinary imperf. is not intended by the Masora in all these cases, and whether consequently {{GHGheb|text=יוֹסִף}}, &c., should not be restored.—On {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־תָחוֹס עֵֽינְךָ}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=11}}, &c., cf. {{GHGpar|72|r}}, according to which {{GHGheb|text=תָחוּס}} should probably be read in every case.—The jussive appears in the place of the cohortative after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=36}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְלֹֽא־נַשְׁאֵר}} co-ordinated with two cohortatives), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=12}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=23}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} ({{GHGheb|text=ונרא}}, i.e. {{GHGheb|text=וְנֵ֫רֶא}}, after another cohortative); also (see above) {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אֹסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=18|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=15}}, and even without {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|109|e}}
2. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} with the jussive (or imperf., cf. {{GHGpar|107|p}}) is used sometimes to express the conviction that something cannot or should not happen; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=9}} (where, however, the text is very doubtful) {{GHGheb|text=וְאַל־תִּשָּׂא לָהֶם|translate=and thou canst not possibly forgive them}} [R.V. ''therefore forgive them not'']; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=34|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=41|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=50|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=121|verse=3|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַל־יִתֵּן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תִּירָא|translate=neither needest thou be afraid}}; 20:17, 40:32.

{{GHGmargin-letter|109|f}}
2. The jussive depending on other moods, or in conditional sentences:

(''a'') Depending<ref>This does not include the cases in which the jussive is not logically dependent on a preceding imperat., but is merely co-ordinated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=27|verse=14}}, &c.</ref> (with {{GHGterm|Wāw}}) on an imperative or cohortative to express an intention or an assurance of a contingent occurrence, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=51}} ''take her and go, and let her be'' ({{GHGheb|text=וּתְהִי}} prop. ''and she will be'')...; 30:3, 31:37, 38:24, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=6}}. Also after interrogative sentences, which include a demand, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=7|verse=2}} (say) ''what is thy desire''..., {{GHGheb|text=וְתֵעָשׂ|translate=and it shall}} (i.e. in order that it may) ''be granted!'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=34}}f. Depending on a cohortative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=אִמָּֽלְטָה נָּא שָׁ֫מָּה|translate=oh, let me escape thither}}...{{GHGheb|text=וּתְחִי נַפְשִׁי}} ''that my soul may live;'' even after a simple imperf. (cf. below, ''g''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=33}} ''whosoever would, he consecrated him'' ... {{GHGheb|text=וִיהִי|translate=that he might be a priest}} (read {{GHGheb|text=כֹּהֵן}}) ''of the high places'', but probably the LXX reading {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}} is to be preferred.<section end=par109 /><noinclude>
